signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Unwind
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.53, having broken decisively below its SMA20/50 cluster at 161.34/162.53. The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard confirms a massive bilateral divergence with JPY outperforming (+1.661%) and USD lagging (-1.375%), creating a 3.036% spread that signals a major regime shift. Despite a 275bp OIS carry advantage for USD, the pair is collapsing as specs (COT JPY net short -114,030) are forced to cover ahead of the BoJ meeting. Options markets are pricing in further downside protection with a moderate put skew (25d RR -1.38) and negative VRP (-0.6%), suggesting realized volatility is outpacing option premiums. JPY safe-haven function is engaging as the bear steepener in the US yield curve (+44.3bp 2s10s) signals growth concerns. Risk: BoJ delivers a dovish hold, allowing the 275bp carry advantage to reassert control and squeeze the pair back toward 161.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — CPI Headline + Positioning + Vol
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1518 following Eurozone Core CPI unexpectedly accelerating to 2.5%, which reinforces ECB hawkishness and a potential September hike. This headline surprise coincides with a technical breakout above the SMA20/50 cluster (1.1424/1.1487), though the pair remains below the SMA200 at 1.1635. Speculative positioning (COT) remains heavily net short at -80,570 (32.4% long), creating a significant short-squeeze runway if the ECB's hawkish bias persists. The options market is already pricing this risk with a 2.7-point Vol Risk Premium (IV 7.1% vs HV30 4.4%), indicating high demand for upside protection. While the 135bp USD carry advantage remains a structural headwind, the ESI (+9.7) suggests Eurozone data momentum is diverging favorably from the neutral US trend. Risk: Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East triggers broad USD safe-haven demand, overriding the CPI-driven ECB repricing.

signals.title: NZD/USD — ESI Outperformance + Retail Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD is trading at 0.5883, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5786/0.5826) after a strong 1W gain of +1.89%. The pair is supported by a significant Economic Surprise Index (ESI) lead of +30.6, the second-highest in the G10, confirming that real-world data is outperforming RBNZ's accommodative real rate of -1.56%. A clear multi-layer divergence is forming: COT specs are heavily net short (-31,649, only 12% long), while retail sentiment has reached a 62% short bias. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The 125bp USD carry advantage remains the primary obstacle to a sustained break above 0.6000. Risk: US NFP surprise reinforces the Fed's 'higher for longer' stance, revitalizing the USD carry bid.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Carry Neutrality + Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD holds at 1.3459, positioned above its entire SMA cluster (SMA200 at 1.3399), as the BoE holds at 3.75%. The OIS carry differential is effectively neutral (-8bp favors GBP), removing the usual USD-centric carry pressure seen elsewhere in G10. Speculative positioning is moderately long (lev_net +33,812), but the options market is expressing extreme caution with a +5.0% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.0%). This high VRP suggests traders are paying a significant premium for protection against a sharp move, likely reflecting uncertainty around the recent BoE communication and high UK 10Y yields at 5.08%. The bear steepener in US yields provides a backdrop of general USD fragility that benefits GBP in a carry-neutral environment. Risk: A break below the SMA200 at 1.3399 triggers a liquidation of the spec long position.
